summary.text: One of the fifty daughters of Danaus by Memphis — paired without lots to Sthenelus son of Egyptus by Tyria when the sons of Aegyptus married the Danaids at Argos; to be kept distinct from Sthenele daughter of Acastus, mother of Patroclus.

story.text: Apollodorus says the three sons of Egyptus by Tyria took as wives, without drawing lots, the daughters of Danaus by Memphis in virtue of the similarity of their names — Sthenelus got Sthenele among the pairings named before the mass slaughter of the wedding night.
